title: Projective-bundle morphisms are preserved by arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $a:S^{\prime}\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose $f$ is projective in the projective-bundle convention [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]: for some finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal E$ [pqf-def-coherent], $X$ admits a closed immersion over $S$ into $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $X\times_SS^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is projective in the same convention. No Noetherianity, flatness, local freeness of $\mathcal E$, or ampleness assumption on either base is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02V6, lemma-base-change-projective, projective case (not merely H-projective).

proof.text: Choose the finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal E$ and an $S$-closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$ supplied by the projective-bundle definition. Put $\mathcal E^{\prime}=a^*\mathcal E$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence and finite type by the two cited pullback statements, applied to the arbitrary scheme morphism $a$. Thus $P^{\prime}=\mathbf P_{S^{\prime}}(\mathcal E^{\prime})$ is an allowed projective bundle for that definition.

source.place: Tag 02V6, lemma-base-change-projective, proof; details via Constructions Tag 01OA, section-projective-bundle, quotient-functor discussion following Definition 01OB.

proof.text: We identify $P^{\prime}$ with $Q=P\times_S S^{\prime}$ explicitly using the quotient classification, which is stated for every quasi-coherent module. Write $p:P\to S$, $p^{\prime}:P^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ and $u:Q\to P$, $v:Q\to S^{\prime}$. Pull back the universal quotient of $P$ along $u$. Via $(pu)^*\mathcal E=(av)^*\mathcal E\cong v^*a^*\mathcal E$, the resulting line quotient determines $b:Q\to P^{\prime}$ over $S^{\prime}$. Conversely the universal quotient of $P^{\prime}$, regarded through $(ap^{\prime})^*\mathcal E\cong(p^{\prime})^*a^*\mathcal E$, determines an $S$-map $c:P^{\prime}\to P$. Its pair with $p^{\prime}$ determines $t:P^{\prime}\to Q$. These quotients and their classification under arbitrary pullback are precisely those of the cited quotient-geometry statement; the composite-pullback identifications are those of module pullback.

source.place: Tag 02V6, lemma-base-change-projective, proof; details via Constructions Tag 01OA, section-projective-bundle, quotient-functor discussion following Definition 01OB.

proof.text: The quotient classified by $bt:P^{\prime}\to P^{\prime}$ is the original universal quotient on $P^{\prime}$: first the definition of $b$ pulls back the quotient on $P$, and then the definition of $c$ identifies its pullback with that on $P^{\prime}$. The natural bijection of the quotient classification therefore gives $bt=\mathrm{id}_{P^{\prime}}$. Likewise $cb:Q\to P$ classifies the pullback by $u$ of the quotient on $P$, so $cb=u$. Also $p^{\prime}b=v$. Hence the two projections of $tb$ are $u$ and $v$, and uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property gives $tb=\mathrm{id}_Q$. Consequently $b$ is an isomorphism over $S^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 02V6, lemma-base-change-projective, proof; details via Constructions Tag 01OA, section-projective-bundle, quotient-functor discussion following Definition 01OB.

proof.text: The square with horizontal arrows $X\times_S S^{\prime}\to X$ and $Q\to P$ and vertical arrows induced by $i$ is cartesian: a map into its pullback is exactly a pair of maps to $X$ and $S^{\prime}$ with equal composites to $S$. Thus the map $j:X\times_S S^{\prime}\to Q$ is a base change of $i$, and is a closed immersion by the cited closed-immersion base-change lemma. Composing with $b$ gives a closed immersion into $P^{\prime}$: postcomposing with a scheme isomorphism preserves the closed-subspace condition and the surjectivity of the structure-sheaf map in the definition of closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 02V6, lemma-base-change-projective, proof; details via Constructions Tag 01OA, section-projective-bundle, quotient-functor discussion following Definition 01OB.

proof.text: The map $bj$ is over $S^{\prime}$, and its target is $\mathbf P_{S^{\prime}}(a^*\mathcal E)$ with $a^*\mathcal E$ finite type and quasi-coherent by step 1. These are exactly the witness and closed embedding required for $X\times_S S^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ to be projective in the projective-bundle convention.
